audit_findings.title: FY2026 owner earnings may include a nonrecurring cash-tax windfall
audit_findings.magnitude: Cash taxes paid fell by $78.713 million, from $117.581 million in FY2025 to $38.868 million in FY2026; FY2026 also recorded $126.032 million of deferred tax expense. Exact valuation impact is unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: Temporarily low cash taxes increase FY2026 OE and can raise the log-trend anchor, which scales forecast OE, terminal value, and equity value.
audit_findings.evidence: However, the Company had a significant reduction in cash tax payments and income taxes payable for the current fiscal year as well as a decrease in deferred tax assets related to the key provisions cited above.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates a significant tax-timing benefit and a large shift into deferred taxes. The $78.713 million year-over-year cash-tax reduction equals 17.4% of FY2026 OE and 18.2% of the $432.1 million anchor, so it is reasonably capable of materially changing normalized OE. Whether, and by how much, the supplied OE calculation captured this benefit remains unresolved; the below-actual trend anchor provides some protection but does not establish immateriality.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct FY2026 recurring cash taxes excluding deductions for previously capitalized R&D and other transition items, revise the historical OE series consistently for later reversals, and rerun the trend anchor and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: New contractual operating costs may be absent from the historical OE run rate
audit_findings.magnitude: $94.146 million over FY2027-FY2029, or $31.382 million annually; the total equals 1.38% of the $6.801 billion base equity value before tax and discounting.
audit_findings.mechanism: Any genuinely incremental, unmodeled payments reduce forecast OE during FY2027-FY2029; they are operating costs rather than an equity-bridge debt deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Included in off-balance sheet contractual purchase obligations were a renewing customer agreement, server and cloud enrollment agreement, and a volume licensing agreement that were signed in June 2026 and together added $94,146 to contractual obligations spread evenly over the next three fiscal years beginning in fiscal 2027.
audit_findings.explanation: The obligations are demonstrated, but their omission from forecasts and their incremental cost after associated revenue or replacement of existing arrangements are not demonstrated. Even treating the entire filed three-year amount as an incremental dollar-for-dollar reduction gives an undiscounted pre-tax exposure of only 1.38% of base equity value, insufficient to change the valuation conclusion. No perpetual cost beyond the disclosed term can be inferred from the record.
audit_findings.action: Map the $31.382 million annual payments into FY2027-FY2029 forecasts, identify replaced contracts and related revenue, and confirm that only net incremental after-tax costs affect OE.

audit_findings.title: Event-driven deconversion income may be receiving a recurring growth multiple
audit_findings.magnitude: FY2026 deconversion revenue less identified costs was $29.952 million versus $27.663 million in FY2025; the FY2026 amount equals 6.9% of the $432.1 million anchor. Lost recurring earnings and exact valuation impact are unquantified.
audit_findings.mechanism: Including unusually high net deconversion fees in normalized OE and growing them increases forecast OE and terminal value, while omitted earnings lost after client departures would also overstate growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Deconversion fees are amounts due from the early termination of our Private and Public Cloud, Processing Services and long-term On-premise Support contracts.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates that deconversion fees are termination-driven and that FY2026 contained $29.952 million of identified net pre-tax contribution. It does not establish the sustainable level, the amount embedded in each historical OE observation, or the recurring earnings lost with terminated clients. The two disclosed years show only a $2.289 million increase, but the total contribution is large enough relative to the anchor that materiality cannot be dismissed without the longer history and client-loss economics.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct net deconversion contribution for every OE year, estimate post-termination recurring margin lost by cohort, normalize the historical series, and rerun the anchor and growth scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Non-current investments appear omitted from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $33.460 million carrying value, equal to $0.475 per diluted share and 0.49% of base equity value.
audit_findings.mechanism: If the investments are separable non-operating assets and their income is excluded from OE, their realizable value should be added through the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: At June 30, 2026, and 2025, the Company had $ 33,460 and $ 25,750 in non-current investments, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge's zero stakes amount omits a demonstrated $33.460 million carrying value, although the filing does not establish that the investments are non-operating or realizable at cost. Even adding the full carrying amount would increase base value by only about $0.48 per share, from $96.50 to approximately $96.98, and would not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the investment schedule, classify each holding, trace its income treatment in OE, determine realizable value, and add only qualifying non-operating value to the bridge.

audit_findings.title: The diluted share count mixes reporting dates
audit_findings.magnitude: The valuation adds 0.361 million June 30 units to 70.112608 million August 12 common shares, a 0.51% increment; removing all 0.361 million would raise base value by approximately $0.50 per share.
audit_findings.mechanism: Double-counted settled awards overstate the denominator and understate per-share value, while PSU payouts above the assumed level could understate the denominator and overstate per-share value.
audit_findings.evidence: As of August 12, 2026, the Registrant had 70,112,608 shares of Common Stock outstanding ($0.01 par value).
audit_findings.explanation: The mixed-date construction is demonstrated, but actual intervening settlements and PSU payout levels are unresolved. The entire known 0.361 million-unit increment is only 0.51% of the August common-share count; even removing it completely would move base value from $96.50 to about $97.00 per share, which cannot change the valuation conclusion. Any additional PSU payout exposure is unquantified but would have to be unusually disproportionate to overturn this scale assessment.
audit_findings.action: Roll each June 30 RSU and PSU tranche to August 12, remove awards already issued into common shares, apply contractual PSU payout ranges and treasury-share treatment where appropriate, and recompute per-share values using a single-date denominator.
